 New restrictions for SNAP recipients begin Sunday 
 Allen Wallace

 Candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages will no longer be allowed for purchase with SNAP benefits in South Carolina beginning Nov. 1.
 The change comes with the launch of the Healthy Food SC project . The project is a two-year initiative which, according to a statement from the South Carolina Department of Social Services, is "designed to help households receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits make healthier food choices."
 SNAP benefits can still be used to buy diet soft drinks, coffee, tea, cereal and baking items, as well as dairy products, bread, fruit, vegetables, meat, poultry and seafood.
 Items such as tobacco, alcohol, paper products and pet food were already banned for use with SNAP benefits.
 For more information on the changes, visit the Department of Social Services website .
